2  JUDGMENT 1.

In respect of an accident which is not in dispute, which resulted in the death of Smt.Karibasamma,
a 61 year old, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums:
Compensation Sl.
As awarded by No. Nature of Heads the Tribunal (In Rs.)

1. Loss of estate 2,52,000/-
Loss of love and affection in 2. 40,000/-
Funeral expenses &
3. 30,000/-
Transportation charges Total 3,22,000/-
2.

The present appeal is filed by the claimants, who are four major sons of deceased Karibasamma,
contending that the denial of compensation to them under the head of loss of dependency, on the ground that they were not dependent on the deceased, cannot be sustained.

3. They placed reliance on the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Birender, 2020 SCC ONLINE SC 28 which has been relied upon by a Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.118 of 2018 (MV-D) [Smt.Lathamma and others vs. Mohammed Saleem, disposed of on 26.03.2021].
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of this judgment of the Apex Court followed by a Division Bench of this Court, it is clear that even the major children would be entitled to claim compensation on the ground that they were dependents of the deceased.
Consequently, the finding recorded by the Tribunal in this regard is set aside.

5. It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 25.07.2016,
Karibasamma, a 61 year old died.
It is also not in dispute that the Insurer is liable to pay the compensation as the offending vehicle was insured.

6. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence adduced before it, has come to the conclusion that the rider of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident which has resulted in the death of Karibasamma.
7. In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

In cases where there is no evidence to determine the actual income, it is Korishetti Hanumanthappa vs Basavaraj S on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16943303/
3 appropriate to adopt the notional income as assessed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which for the year 2016 would be Rs.9,500/-.
8.
The age of the deceased has been determined by the Tribunal as 61 years based on the age mentioned in the voters ID card.
9. The learned counsel for the claimants, however, pointed out to the fact that in the post-mortem report, the age of the deceased is recorded as 55 years.
10. In my view, it would be appropriate to accept the findings recorded by the Tribunal, since it is based on the age shown in the Voters ID card, which normally would be given by the voter himself.
11. As the deceased was aged 61 years, future prospects cannot be added.
12. Out of the said sum of Rs.9,500/-, 1/3rd of the same (Rs.3,167/-) would have to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased, as the deceased was 61 years old.
The net income will be Rs.6,333/-.

13. As the deceased was aged 61 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121,
a multiplier of '7' would have to be applied.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
14. Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.5,31,972/- (Rs.6,333/- x 12 x '7')
towards "loss of dependency" as against Rs.2,52,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of estate.

15. The claimants being the four major sons of the deceased, each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of love and affection" i.e., in all Rs.1,76,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".
16.

Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :
Compensation Sl.

As awarded by No. Nature of Heads this Court (In Rs.) Loss of Dependency 1. 5,31,972/-
(Rs.6,333/- x 12 x '7')

2. Loss of love and affection 1,76,000/-
3. Conventional heads 33,000/-
 Total 7,40,972/-

sentences.text: Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.7,40,972/- as against Rs.3,22,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
18. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
19. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded along with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
